subject: Next steps for Globomart POC — scope, evaluation plan & model fallback
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@globomart.com>, Aaron Lin <aaron.lin@globomart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-19T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + proposed POC charter (multilingual support & model fallback)

Hi Priya / Aaron —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed starter charter for the POC so we can move to scheduling and scoping. I summarized the high-level asks below and put owners against each deliverable.

What you told us (priority):
- Customer-facing summarization across product pages (EN, ES, PT-BR, FR) is the highest priority.
- Strong quality on domain-specific terminology (retail SKUs, promotions) is required.
- Latency expectations: <300ms p95 for single-item queries, faster for small summaries.
- Migrations: the solution must fall back to a smaller, cheaper model in the event of capacity/latency pressure.
- Security: no persistent storage of raw customer submissions outside of allowed logs; audit evidence required.

Proposed POC success criteria (draft):
1) Accuracy: human-rated relevance >= 85% on a 250-example eval set per locale.
2) Robustness: multi-turn coherence score >= 80% on dialogue checks.
3) Latency: 95th percentile token latency < 300ms for EN baseline traffic profile.
4) Cost: per-1k-token inference cost within 30% of agreed benchmark.
5) Rollback/fallback: automated routing to fallback model under load with <2% user-visible errors.

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Dataset: Globomart will provide a sample set (250 examples per language) + 50 adversarial prompts per locale.
- Metrics: human ratings (accuracy/relevance), rouge/bertscore for automated checks, latency traces from Redwood console.
- Model test matrix: primary candidate + 2 fallback variants (see model shortlist below).

Model shortlist (initial recommendation):
- Primary: Llama-2-Chat-13B (quantized fp16) — good cost/quality balance for product-summarization with strong instruction-following.
- Secondary (fallback): Mistral-7B-8bit — inexpensive, fast; to be used when routing policy triggers (regional capacity or cost cap).
- Multilingual augmentation: add a localized fine-tune / prompt-shortlist for ES/PT/FR; if time permits, test Llama-2-13B-ft-localized on a small validation fold.

Timeline (proposal):
- Jan 20: Globomart provides sample dataset + initial acceptance criteria. (Owner: Priya)
- Jan 23: Redwood delivers POC charter + config (batches, kv-cache policy, billing estimate). (Owner: Lauren)
- Jan 26–30: Model runs & automated evals + first human ratings pass (Owners: Karthik / Dylan)
- Feb 2: Joint review, go/no-go on canary.

Attachments: I attached a draft POC scope and a simple eval checklist.

Action items for this thread:
- Priya: confirm dataset delivery date and success metric acceptance (reply here).
- Aaron: share any regulatory constraints affecting logs/audit.
- Karthik/Dylan: I want you to confirm feasibility of the 300ms p95 target for the sample traffic once we have dataset.

Happy to hop on a short sync this week to finalize dates — propose Jan 21 10am PT if that works.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: globomart-poc-scope-draft.pdf (application/pdf), poc-eval-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Priya Shah <priya@globomart.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Lin <aaron.lin@globomart.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-19T11:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed POC charter (multilingual support & model fallback)

Thanks Lauren — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset: we can deliver the 250 examples per language by Jan 22 EOD. We'll include canonical product descriptions and a set of customer query logs (sanitized).
2) Success metrics: the accuracy/relevance threshold of 85% is fine; would like to add a business SLA around hallucination tolerance — max 2% critical hallucinations (claims about pricing/availability that are verifiably false).
3) Latency: 300ms p95 is aggressive for multi-region traffic; can we define that as a US-only target for the POC and then measure EU separately?
4) Fallback behavior: prefer that fallback responses indicate degraded mode to the customer (single sentence) rather than silent substitution.

We can make Jan 21 10am PT — Aaron and I are available. Also, can you confirm whether the fallback model will preserve the same prompt engineering / guardrails, or if it will use a simplified prompt to save tokens?

Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Product, Globomart
priya@globomart.com
+1 (206) 555-1123

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@globomart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-19T12:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed POC charter (multilingual support & model fallback)

Great points, Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Responses inline: 

1) Dataset: Jan 22 works. We'll confirm receipt and a quick sampling sanity check the same day.
2) Hallucination SLA: adding a 2% critical-hallucination cap is reasonable. We'll include a manual adjudication step in the eval checklist and add that to the success criteria.
3) Latency: we can scope the p95 <300ms to US traffic for the POC and record EU metrics separately. We'll include regional traces in the console.
4) Fallback behavior: agreed — fallback responses will include a short flag line ("Note: limited mode — results may be abbreviated") and we will preserve guardrail layers. To save cost, the fallback model will use a simplified system prompt + fewer retrieval steps; we will report on any quality delta in the joint review.

Model note: Karthik / Dylan — please confirm feasibility of preserving the same guardrail checks (safety filters + retrieval re-rank) when routing to Mistral-7B-8bit fallback. If there are any features that won't be supported in fallback mode (e.g., heavy retrieval + reranking), call them out so we can set expectations with Globomart.

I'll slot Jan 21 10am PT on the calendars and share a short agenda.

Thanks,
Lauren

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@globomart.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-21T14:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed POC charter (multilingual support & model fallback)

Hi all — quick technical note following Lauren's ask. Short answers first: yes, we can preserve guardrails and most retrieval flows on the Mistral-7B fallback, but there are trade-offs.

Details:
- Safety/filters: yes, same filter chain can run pre- and post-model. No functional regression expected.
- Retrieval: we can keep retrieval, but to hit target latency on the fallback we recommend: 1) fewer retrieved passages (top-3 instead of top-10), 2) smaller embedding model for nearest-neighbor lookups in fallback mode. We'll quantify the delta in the Feb 2 review.
- Prompting: fallback will use a simplified system prompt to reduce token count; expect a 3-7 point drop in human-rated relevance in early tests (we will measure).
- Quantization: Mistral-7B will be run in an 8-bit path; we will validate hallucination rates in the initial run.

Action items from Eng:
- Dylan: stand up the two-model test harness and produce an automated comparison report (English + Spanish) by Jan 30.
- Karthik: prepare a short doc on expected cost delta and latency forecasts for primary vs fallback models by Jan 23.

I'll be on the Jan 21 sync and can walk through the trade-offs.

-Karthik
Head of Applied ML, Redwood Inference
